title: Platform systems & services — team wiki, runbooks, dashboards, and roadmap (Q2 2026)
author: Alex Chen
body:
Overview:

This page is the canonical team wiki entry for Redwood's Platform Systems & Services team. It consolidates: systems inventory, ownership, key dashboards and alerting rules, operational runbooks, recent retrospectives, and the roadmap for Q2 2026. Use this as the first stop for onboarding, incident response, and planning.

Scope:
- Applies to the Platform Systems & Services team (infra, ops, dashboards, runbooks).
- Covers internal platform components: control-plane services, observability stack, CI/CD, cluster provisioning, and core platform automation.
- Does NOT include model-serving runtime internals (see eng-serving-runtime).

Quick links:
- Oncall roster: https://company-pager.example/internal/oncall/platform
- Pager duty: PD schedule "platform-oncall"
- Dashboards home: Grafana -> "Platform / Overview"

## Systems inventory (top-level)
A concise list of systems we operate with owner and SLO summary. For full config and infra-as-code references, see the linked repo in each row.

| Service | Purpose | Owner | 90-day SLO | Infra repo |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|
| platform-control-plane | Central orchestration for routing and routing policies | platform-core | 99.95% availability | git://infra/platform-control-plane
| ci-cd | Build and release pipelines (builders, runners) | ci-platform | 99% successful pipeline start | git://infra/ci-cd
| observability | Metrics, logs, traces (Prometheus/Grafana/Tempo/Elasticsearch) | observability | 99.9% scrape/ingest | git://infra/observability
| fleet-manager | GPU fleet capacity and autoscaling | infra-fleet | 99.5% API availability | git://infra/fleet-manager
| config-service | Central config/feature flags | platform-core | 99.99% read availability | git://infra/config-service

Notes: owners are the primary escalation contact; secondary contacts are listed in the service README in the infra repo.

## Dashboards & alerts — structure and key rules
Purpose: dashboards provide an at-a-glance health check; alerts map to runbooks and oncall.

Dashboards (Grafana):
- Platform / Overview: CPU, memory, API latency P50/P95/P99, error rates, ingress QPS, downstream queue length.
- Observability / Ingest: scraping lag, indexing pipeline backpressure, ES JVM/heap.
- Fleet / Capacity: GPU utilization by pool, pending pods, scheduling latency.
- CI / Pipelines: runner queue length, job start latency, failure rate by project.

Alerting conventions (Prometheus Alertmanager):
- Severity labels: sev:critical | sev:high | sev:medium | sev:low.
- Pager routing: sev:critical -> primary oncall + ops manager, sev:high -> primary oncall only.
- Alert annotations include: runbook link, playbook steps, escalation path.

Key alerts and thresholds (examples):
| Alert name | Trigger | Initial notify | Runbook |
|---|---|---|---|
| PlatformAPIHighErrorRate | api_errors_rate > 5% for 5m | sev:critical | /runbooks/platform-api-high-error-rate
| PrometheusIngestBacklog | remote_write_backlog > 1h | sev:high | /runbooks/observability-ingest-backlog
| GPUProvisionFailure | provision_failures > 3 in 10m | sev:critical | /runbooks/fleet-provision-failure
| CICDPipelineQueueGrowth | queued_jobs > 100 for 10m | sev:medium | /runbooks/ci-queue-growth

## Runbooks — canonical quick-play steps
Each runbook follows the same format: summary, impact, detection, mitigation steps, post-incident actions, owner. Short links to the runbooks are stored in the infra repo and in this wiki.

Example runbook excerpt: Platform API: high error rate
1) Triage
   - Check Grafana > Platform / Overview for API error trends (5m, 1h).
   - Use traces (Tempo) to identify top error types and endpoints.
2) Mitigate
   - If a rollout is implicated, rollback the latest canary (CI tag -> previous stable).
   - If backend dependency is slow, enable fail-open cached responses (config-service flag).
   - Scale the API deployment by +2 replicas (kubectl scale deploy platform-api --replicas=N+2) and increase request concurrency limits.
3) Escalate
   - If errors persist >15 minutes after mitigation, page the oncall-exec and platform-core owner.
4) Postmortem
   - Create postmortem within 48 hours, include timelines and action items.

Full runbooks (links):
- /runbooks/platform-api-high-error-rate
- /runbooks/observability-ingest-backlog
- /runbooks/fleet-provision-failure
- /runbooks/ci-queue-growth

## Oncall process and rotation
- Schedule: 1 primary (week), 1 secondary (week), 1 escalation engineer (rotating).
- Handoff checklist (every handoff):
  1. Review open alerts in Alertmanager.
  2. Check red/amber dashboards for any degrading signals.
  3. Confirm contactability via Slack and PagerDuty.
- After an incident: runbook author updates and a blameless retrospective within 7 days.

## Incident response checklist (high level)
1) Acknowledge alert in PagerDuty within 5 minutes.
2) Triage impact and scope; update incident channel (#platform-incident-[id]).
3) Execute mitigation runbook steps; mark steps in the incident timeline.
4) If sev:critical, call the incident bridge (Zoom ID in runbook).
5) Declare incident severity and engage exec escalation if recovery >30 minutes.
6) Run post-incident review and assign action owners.

## Retrospectives & continuous improvement
Process:
- For every sev:critical incident, host a blameless retro within 7 calendar days.
- Use the standard template: timeline, root cause analysis, action items (owner + due date), follow-up check-in 30 days after.

Recent retro summary (Q1 2026):
- Incident: Prometheus ingestion backlog (2026-02-03)
  - Root cause: misconfigured remote_write after a version bump; backpressure on ingest pipeline.
  - Actions: add pre-deploy ingest smoke tests, increase remote_write buffering defaults, update rollout checklist.
  - Owner: Diego Martinez — completed 2026-02-18.

## Roadmap (Q2 2026 high-level milestones)
- Apr 2026: Deploy observability horizontal scaling — reduce scrape lag under high load.
- May 2026: Platform control-plane canary rollout automation (A/B + automatic rollback).
- Jun 2026: Fleet autoscaler improvements for burst capacity (fast spin-up for dedicated pools).
- Ongoing: Runbook coverage — ensure top 30 alerts have runbooks and owner assigned (target completion: 2026-06-30).

Success metrics:
- Reduce mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) for sev:critical to <3 minutes.
- Reduce recurring incidents by 40% quarter-over-quarter via action closure.
- Top-30 alerts all have validated runbooks and owners by end of Q2.

## Platform how-tos (common tasks)
1) Add an alert rule (Prometheus):
   - Edit the alerts.yml in git://infra/observability, add rule with labels and annotations (include runbook link).
   - Open PR and follow CI checks (unit test + alert linting).
   - After merge, verify firing in Alertmanager UI and update Grafana dashboard if necessary.

Example alert snippet:
```yaml
- alert: PlatformAPIHighErrorRate
  expr: sum(rate(platform_api_errors_total[5m])) / sum(rate(platform_api_requests_total[5m])) > 0.05
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: critical
  annotations:
    runbook: /runbooks/platform-api-high-error-rate
    summary: "Platform API error rate >5% (5m)"
```

2) Scale a deployment temporarily (kubectl):
```bash
kubectl -n platform scale deployment/platform-api --replicas=6
# Observe pods: kubectl get pods -n platform -l app=platform-api
```

3) Runbook validation (playbook):
   - Schedule a runbook playthrough with oncall and 2 engineers quarterly.
   - Record the exercise, update the runbook with gaps and timelines.

## Documentation & team wiki hygiene
- When creating or changing runbooks, maintain a changelog entry in the runbook file (author, date, change summary).
- Annual review: owners must review their service page and runbooks at least once per 12 months.
- Tag pages with labels: service, runbook, owner, year.
